_readme: Single source of truth for the homepage bench table, tested picks, 'on our radar' list, ticker and cost calculator. To publish a new hands-on review: add an entry to 'tested' (newest first), put a 480x640 card image at images/card_<slug>.webp, and run node build.js. ptt = measured PTT delay text, or null if not timed. cost = {hw: per-radio USD, renew: per-radio per-year USD after year 1, src: where the fee came from} or null if not confirmed.

tested.name: Radtel P8
tested.bestAt: Clear, loud audio and a solid zinc-alloy body
tested.watchOut: 1–2 s PTT delay; no published IP rating
tested.desc: Clear, loud audio and a body that feels premium for the price, with SIMs included for the first year (about $10 per card per year after, per Radtel). Expect a 1 to 2 second pause after you press PTT.

cost.src: Radtel: 2-pack from ~$99; about $10 per SIM per year after year 1

faq: Does the Radtel P8 need a subscription?

The SIM is included for the first year. After that Radtel quotes about $10 per SIM per year, with the GXIN platform advertised as free for life. You can also buy it without a SIM and use your own AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon SIM.
What is the Radtel P8's range?
Anywhere both radios have 4G LTE signal, so it can reach across the country. With no cell signal it can't talk at all; it has no off-network mode.
How much delay does the Radtel P8 have?
We measured about 1 to 2 seconds between pressing PTT and the other radio hearing us, slower than Radtel's claimed 0.3 to 1 second. Pause a beat after pressing the button.
Is the Radtel P8 waterproof?
Radtel claims water resistance but publishes no IP rating, so don't assume it survives heavy rain or submersion.

tested.name: ChoYong WT2
tested.cat: Handheld · PoC + UHF + SW/AM/FM + internet radio
tested.bestAt: PoC, analog UHF, shortwave and internet radio in one
tested.watchOut: Use 2.4 GHz WiFi for PoC; compact for big hands
tested.desc: A PoC radio, a 2W analog UHF walkie-talkie and a TEF6686 shortwave/AM/FM receiver with internet radio, all in one handheld. PTT was excellent on 2.4 GHz WiFi; the analog UHF side is weak, as expected at 2W.
faq: Does the ChoYong WT2 need a SIM card?
No SIM is listed in the box. In our testing PoC worked over WiFi, and PTT was excellent on 2.4 GHz WiFi rather than 5 GHz.
Can the ChoYong WT2 receive shortwave?
Yes. It has a TEF6686-based shortwave, AM and FM receiver. Reception is good with an external loop antenna, AM is impressively sensitive and FM was flawless in our testing.
Does the WT2 work with no internet?
Its analog UHF side transmits at 2 W radio-to-radio with no network. It's a short-range safety net, weak as you'd expect at 2 W.

tested.name: OMIZN M9
tested.bestAt: Rugged aluminum body, great sound, readable screen
tested.watchOut: Heavy at 300 g; no public group directory
tested.desc: An aluminum alloy body and dust-proof, noise-reducing speaker that earn the outdoor pitch, with great sound and an easy-to-read screen. It is heavier than most, and there is no public directory for finding other users.
faq: Does the OMIZN M9 need a subscription?
The SIM is pre-installed and OMIZN's manual says first-year SIM and data fees are covered. A renewal service is offered after that, but OMIZN doesn't publish the price.
Is the OMIZN M9 rugged?
It has an aluminum alloy body and a dust-proof, noise-reducing speaker, and it felt solid in our testing. At about 300 g it's heavier than most PoC radios.
Can you meet other users on the OMIZN M9?
There's no public group directory, so it's best for closed groups such as a family or a work team that sets up its own group.

tested.name: TIDRADIO TD-M2 Pro
tested.bestAt: Two PTT buttons: nationwide PoC plus local FRS
tested.watchOut: Odmaster app is buggy; groups are hard to find
tested.desc: The cheapest way into dual-mode: PTT1 talks over LTE nationwide, PTT2 drops to license-free FRS when there is no signal. Solid in hand with clear audio. The Odmaster app is the weak spot.

cost.src: TIDRADIO: first year free, published $9.99 per year after

faq: Does the TIDRADIO TD-M2 Pro need a subscription?
The SIM ships pre-activated with the first year free and 800 MB per month. After that TIDRADIO publishes a renewal of $9.99 per year.
Does the TD-M2 Pro work without cell service?
Yes. PTT2 talks on license-free FRS radio-to-radio with no SIM or network, while PTT1 uses 4G PoC. Both stay active at the same time.
What app does the TD-M2 Pro use?
TIDRADIO's Odmaster app, which also runs its other PoC radios. In our testing the app was buggy and finding existing groups was hard, so expect some setup time.

tested.name: Wouxun KG-WV9
tested.bestAt: Group and member calling built into the radio menu
tested.watchOut: Not sold through US retail; quote-only
tested.desc: Group and member calling run from the radio's own menu, with no app needed mid-call, backed by Wouxun's long two-way radio track record. Ordered direct from Wouxun or a distributor.
faq: Where can you buy the Wouxun KG-WV9?
It's sold direct from Wouxun or through distributors rather than US retail like Amazon, so pricing is by quote.
Does the KG-WV9 need an app for calls?
No. Group and member calling run from the radio's own menu. The menu feels more like a traditional two-way radio than a smartphone.
Does the Wouxun KG-WV9 have GPS and SOS?
Yes, it lists built-in GPS (platform-dependent) and a dedicated SOS function.

tested.name: CARRBORG X13
tested.bestAt: Bright screen, clear audio, no data subscription
tested.watchOut: More PTT lag than faster rivals; large body
tested.desc: A genuinely bright, easy-to-read screen and clear voice audio, with lifetime free data that undercuts most rivals on long-term cost. A touch more PTT lag than faster radios, and a big body for small hands.

cost.src: Seller listing: lifetime free data included

faq: Does the CARRBORG X13 have a monthly fee?
No. It's sold with a pre-activated SIM and lifetime free data, so the purchase price is the whole cost, as long as the seller's service continues.
Is the CARRBORG X13 fast to key up?
It has a touch more PTT lag than faster PoC radios in our testing. Fine for casual and team use, noticeable in quick back-and-forth.
Is the CARRBORG X13 good for small hands?
It's a large handheld. The upside is a genuinely bright, easy-to-read screen.
